candidate.answerReason: E is the only listed price satisfying both strict conditions: nine copies cost $9.99 and ten cost $11.10. Every other choice makes ten copies cost at most $11.00.

methods.label: Check the listed prices
methods.explanation:
Choices A through D all cost at most \(\$1.10\) per copy. At any of those prices, ten copies cost at most
\[
10\cdot\$1.10=\$11.00.
\]
Thus none satisfies the requirement that ten copies cost more than \(\$11.00\); equality is not enough.

For choice E, the two costs are
\[
9\cdot\$1.11=\$9.99<\$10.00,
\]
\[
10\cdot\$1.11=\$11.10>\$11.00.
\]
Both conditions hold, so the only listed price that works is \(\boxed{\$1.11}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses decimal multiplication and comparison of the choices; formal inequality-system solving is unnecessary.
